58e2d5c25024a9d2: NVIDIA on Monday said it was reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO, effective immediately, an extraordinary reversal that followed calls from US President Donald Trump for his return after Huang resigned over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

The reversal, which sent shares soaring 33 per cent, came after the board said it saw no national security risk in the return of Huang, who had also allegedly carried on affairs with at least two Nvidia employees.
Multiple investigations of the company are underway, including by the US SEC and the Department of Justice, related to everything from potential accounting issues to alleged chip smuggling.
Trump, who last week urged Nvidia to bring Huang back after its board ruled out his return, praised the reversal on Monday as the "correct and proper decision."
In a post on Truth Social, Trump said the US government had no reason to believe Huang's return posed a national security risk and had no evidence he had engaged in unlawful conduct.
He nevertheless urged Nvidia to continue investigating the company's compliance with US export controls to ensure it was meeting its obligations to protect national security.
Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones had said last week that the company would not rehire Huang despite a growing campaign for his return.
Huang resigned on Nov 12 following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with a businesswoman whom US authorities suspect of spying for China, an allegation Beijing denies.

Huang built Nvidia from a video-game chip designer into the dominant supplier of artificial-intelligence processors, playing a central role in its chip roadmap, major customer relationships and ties with Washington.

Nvidia said its board voted unanimously on Monday to reinstate Huang after concluding that it was satisfied with his candour and leadership ability. The board said that, after receiving input from senior US government officials, it saw no national security risk from his return.

The board has also formed a committee to investigate whether foreign intelligence efforts targeted Huang and is also starting a search to name a new chief compliance officer. The company said Colette Kress would continue as chief financial officer.

Huang's departure reverberated from Silicon Valley to Taipei and Washington. A petition calling for his reinstatement drew more than 180,000 signatures, including one from Elon Musk, underscoring the unusually strong support for an executive who stepped down amid controversy.
The reversal highlights Huang's deep influence over Nvidia and raises broader questions about how dependent one of the world's most valuable companies remains on its co-founder.

9fe6e27d2189c901: <!--kg-card-end: html--> ARTEX, an open source framework that makes it easy for AI agents to hack companies at superspeed, is causing havoc. People using the tool appear to include Chinese hackers breaking into targets for espionage, and financially-motivated hackers too. Earlier this month, the FBI published a warning to potential targets, and said hackers using ARTEX have targeted government, healthcare, telecommunications, legal, defense, financial services, and semiconductor sectors globally.

ARTEX is written in Go, and all someone needs to do is connect their preferred LLM — from Anthropic, DeepSeek, or whoever — and ARTEX then creates a bunch of agents that are designed to focus on different hacking tasks. There is something qualitatively different about ARTEX when compared to other hacking tools. As the FBI explains, it uses agentic AI to automate much of the hacking process “at machine speed.” This can be reconnaissance — the scoping out of a target to understand their infrastructure — right up to actually hacking a target and stealing their data. An AI agent doesn’t need to sleep, eat, or commute home. ARTEX can complete an entire hack in just a few hours from start to finish, the FBI says. With a tool like ARTEX, a hacker can set up the tool and let it rip. As Google’s threat intelligence arm has noted, hackers are using other similar multi-agent frameworks like CAIRN, CyberStrikeAI, and PentAGI too.

Do you know anything else about ARTEX or related breaches? I would love to hear from you. Using a non-work device, you can message me securely on Signal at joseph.404 or send me an email at joseph@404media.co.

The original author of ARTEX, who goes by Autumn-27 and writes in Chinese, took the tool off of GitHub in October. A message left on their GitHub says, “It has come to my attention that the ARTEX tool has recently been misused by malicious actors to carry out cyberattacks. As the creator of ARTEX, I wish to make the following formal statement.” They go on to say they are not associated with these attacks, that malicious use of the tool runs “entirely counter to my original intent,” and that they are moving ARTEX into a closed-source model and will no longer update it.

But ARTEX is already free. Several people have cloned and continue to publish versions of ARTEX that anyone can use, and anyone who already downloaded their copy from Autumn-27 may still have it saved locally. ARTEX is not going anywhere.

“I’m not going to remove the repository,” one person hosting a version of ARTEX, who goes by the handle Racem, told 404 Media. “The code is already copied everywhere, as the advisory notes; deleting this repository would remove the maintained version and its fixes, not the capability.”

Jiwoo Jung, CTO of an AI marketing company and who is also hosting a version of ARTEX on GitHub, said someone asked them to take the tool down. “On November 3, a user opened a public GitHub issue (#61) saying their service had been attacked by someone using ARTEX, and asked that the project be taken down or restricted until safeguards were added,” he told 404 Media in an email. “I replied that the project would stay up, pointing to its authorized-use terms, and suggested they work with law enforcement, which they said they had already contacted.”

<!--kg-card-begin: html--> <!--kg-card-end: html--> Tools being available openly is, of course, the nature of open source software, and specifically penetration testing and cybersecurity tools. For decades, cybersecurity defenders have used offensive open source tools to test their own defenses or those of their clients. This lets them simulate what a hacker might do, and they can patch their systems, hopefully, before a hack. But, these tools can also be used by real attackers. Look at Russian state-sponsored hackers using the age old Metasploit framework.

What has changed is the “speed and the skill level required” to hack, Jung said. “Agentic tooling compresses steps that used to take a skilled operator days into hours. That is why I think defenders need to understand these tools and have detection signatures for them.”

Racem acknowledged the damage that ARTEX is causing. “The harm the [FBI] advisory describes is real, and I don’t minimize it,” they said. “The behaviour it lists (entering systems without authorization, taking data) is a crime, whoever commits it. I’m not going to pretend the tool is harmless: it automates a large part of the manual work of a penetration test, which is why it is useful, and why some people will misuse it. The authorization belongs to the operator, not to the tool.”

The reason Racem is hosting it is for small teams, they said. “I also maintain it for people testing their own systems: founders and small teams without a pentest budget can run it against their own infrastructure for the price of some API calls. I have seen people do that, and I use it myself on bug bounty programs and for AI security research,” Racem said.

Both Racem and Jung said they don’t know if the FBI advisory is talking about their specific versions of ARTEX, and really, they can’t possibly know. But, both admonished malicious use of the tool. “I take it seriously. Using ARTEX against systems without authorization is exactly what the project’s README and legal notice prohibit, and I’d encourage security teams to check their systems against the indicators of compromise the FBI published,” Jung added.
Jung said he has since added an email address people can contact if they think ARTEX was used against their systems.

596a5e896a9199ce: PETALING JAYA: The government has completed tax refunds totalling RM20.271 billion involving 3.65 million taxpayer cases as of Oct 31.
This includes more than RM13 billion paid to companies and micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), Bernama reported.
Inland Revenue Board (LHDN) CEO Abu Tariq Jamaluddin said RM13.036 billion of the total amount had been refunded to 206,234 corporate taxpayers, including MSMEs.

He said LHDN would continue to strengthen tax administration efficiency, particularly in handling tax refunds, implementing e-Invoicing and providing compliance facilities to ensure the country's tax environment remained responsive to the needs of the business community.
Abu Tariq said 2.25 billion e-Invoices had been submitted by more than 270,000 taxpayers as of today.

He said the use of e-Invoice data had helped encourage voluntary tax compliance, with more than 97,000 taxpayers coming forward to submit tax returns for previous years, involving RM1.68 billion in taxes payable.
More than 1.05 million applications had also been received under the Special Voluntary Disclosure Programme for Stamp Duty as of Oct 31, with penalties amounting to RM184 million fully remitted.
He said the programme had been extended until Dec 31, while Phase 2 of the Stamp Duty Self-Assessment System (STSDS) was scheduled to begin on Jan 1, 2027.

To help stamp duty payers transition to the system, Abu Tariq said LHDN was providing penalty exemptions throughout this year for offences involving the submission of inaccurate stamp duty returns (BNDS) under the STSDS.

389ef9f57930983b: PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has warned against any attempt to allow Islam to become a mask for corruption, oppression and the marginalisation of the poor.
He said efforts to strengthen Islamic values must be accompanied by meaningful reforms to address wrongdoing and ensure that the poor and religious educational institutions are not neglected.

"Islam must not become a mask to legitimise misconduct, corruption and oppression while marginalising the poor," he said in his speech at the Khatam Sama' Hadis Antarabangsa 2026 ceremony at Masjid Putra.
Present were Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Datuk Dr Zulkifli Hasan and Grand Mufti of India Sheikh Abu Bakar Ahmad Al-Malibari.
Anwar said Malaysia continued to grapple with the legacy of colonial rule, which had transformed not only its political and educational systems but also the thinking and values of its people.
"After independence, the system changed, but colonial thinking was not necessarily eradicated. This is what we have inherited," he said.
Anwar said reversing the effects of colonialism and restoring Islamic consciousness required time, determination and a willingness to undertake reforms.
"That is why we have found the courage to bring about change. First, we must remember our history, and second, recognise that without inner strength, we cannot bring about any change," he said.
He also highlighted the historical role of madrasahs, tahfiz schools and pondok institutions in safeguarding Islamic teachings and preserving the community's identity during colonial rule.

Anwar said the government had been restoring financial support for these institutions over the past three to four years, with annual increases in allocations to upgrade facilities, some of which had fallen into disrepair.

He said Malaysia must also embrace emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and digitalisation, without compromising its religious values, cultural identity and traditions, stressing that technological progress and major investments alone could not guarantee the nation's strength.

Under the 2027 Budget tabled last month, the government allocated RM200 million to repair and upgrade registered religious schools, tahfiz institutions and pondok schools, while expanding financial assistance to cover their operating costs.

7a9538eb644cd8f3: Have you or someone you love been affected by a tech outage this week? Yeah, us too.

You can listen to the latest episode of The Kettle right here on this page, as well as on Spotify, Apple Music, or YouTube. Those platforms also let you subscribe to The Kettle, so you are always notified when the latest episode goes live

In a week of big stories the biggest one seems to be the fact that everyone from Microsoft to the NSA was dealing with outages, and here's what might be the worst part: It doesn't seem to be AI, nor hostile countries intent on destroying our infrastructure.

Unfortunately for all of us, what the past week of outages reveal is that – as we discussed on The Kettle less than a month ago – all of our essential tech infrastructure is basically held together with duct tape and twine.

Join host Brandon Vigliarolo, cybersecurity editor Jessica Lyons, and open source reporter Liam Proven to discuss what comes next, and whether we can fix any of this without tearing all of it out and starting from scratch.
A lightly edited transcript is included below:

Hi everyone and welcome to the latest episode of the Register's Kettle podcast. I'm your host, Reg reporter Brandon Vigliarolo, and if you're hearing this, then that means there isn't an outage right now, which seems like that might be a lot to ask of our technology in the past week. It's been a busy week. We had Anthropic's IPO, Nvidia drama continuing, and other stuff going on. But the one thing that everyone seems to be talking about is what's become known in the zeitgeist as Outagepalooza, as it seems like everything was offline at some point in the past few days. With me to discuss the chaos and the conspiracy theories they're giving rise to is Reg cybersecurity editor Jessica Lyons and our open source reporter Liam Proven. Guys, what's happening?
I've got my tinfoil hat on right now, so I'm ready.
Yes, I've had family calling me being like, my god, what's happening? Who's ending the world right now? Is it AI?

Wonderful. My mum's wardrobe door stuck this week and we found a company on the little rock in the middle of the Irish Sea that fixes sliding doors and he didn't get my emails because he's one hundred percent Microsoft and he uses Hotmail and it's Hotmail.

And when I got it through, you'd be amazed at the ramifications. I SMS'd him in the end and he got that and then was really angry because I said, "Dude, I've been trying to get you for three days. Can you at least reply and say Friday?" And he's like, "No, I've got no email, I've got no internet, I've got nothing."
My god. Yes, it's been an interesting week. So Jess, catch us up on everything that's fallen apart in the past few days. We've got quite a list growing here.

Yes. Well, we'll start with Outlook. I'm sorry, Microsoft. It was larger than just Outlook, but similar to Liam, I got this message from my dad. We were at dinner with some friends and he said, "What is going on? I haven't been able to access Outlook all day. What is happening?" So this happened last week and there was this massive Microsoft outage and ultimately, people assumed it was maybe a cyber attack. Is somebody DDoSing Microsoft? What's going on? And then a few days later, Microsoft said, "No, this was a faulty software update that we pushed back in July, and it's affecting all of our 365 services now." So that was last Thursday. Then a day later, the FAA grounded all planes.

And again, in light of Microsoft, people were still having problems with Microsoft. All the planes are grounded. At the time, we just knew it was some type of communication error. And that sounds like something that a lot of nation states would really like to hit and attack. And this one, we ultimately learned that it was due to a network upgrade. Their provider, L3Harris, was switching out the copper wiring with fiber. And this has been an ongoing project. Also, kind of seems like maybe Friday the 13th isn't the best day to undertake this.
I hadn't even thought about the fact that it was Friday the 13th that all that happened.

So we see that right after Microsoft. And there was kind of a lull over the weekend, which was nice. But then Monday first thing, customers at Chase and US Bank and other major American banks couldn't withdraw any money from their accounts. And this we find out is also due to a massive outage. Chase later said it was a software bug in an on-premises hardware system, and they said it wasn't a cyber attack. Then the next day, the classified network that the US National Security Agency uses for their internal communications went offline. This is really classified stuff that they are communicating about internally. This went offline and when something at a secretive government agency like the NSA goes offline, immediately the first thought is, "Who's attacking us?" The agency later said this was due to scheduled routine maintenance. And actually I almost forgot: Tuesday, Apple had a bunch of issues. It was affecting different services like Apple Support, iCloud, Apple Pay, and their retail stores. There were people waiting in lines because they had some tech issue that they wanted to get help with, and they're not able to get any help because Apple's offline as well. So we have all these outages at these major agencies and companies over the last week. So everybody automatically goes to, "Who's attacking us? Who is responsible for this?" What people assume to be a massive coordinated cyber attack And that wasn't the case.
Right. In pretty much every instance. Liam, Canonical was having an outage too, right?

Yes. I was going to say, we didn't notice the FAA very much in Europe, but Canonical got hit by a distributed denial of service attack. I probably don't need to spell that out. At the end of last week, just before their now semi-annual Ubuntu Summit, which is when they have a bunch of talks about what's coming up and what's new. They've been hit by a number of attacks before. It was very bad timing. Some of their services stayed up.
So this was actually attributable to an attack though.

I believe in this case it looks like it was another DDoS, but it's not the first time. It's not obvious in the open source world that sometimes big, very visible projects are actually from tiny companies. And sometimes things that don't look so important actually have huge companies behind them. But Canonical is not a very big company. And they're a hundred percent remote company. They don't really have headquarters. There's this lovely office which is part of a floor of one building in London, but not that many people work there. It's all hot desks.

It's relatively easy to take such a distributed company offline. And so it's becoming hard to say whether some of these things really are due to attacks or due to general vulnerabilities that are being maybe not even exploited, just massive scale attempts to exploit them. And it's not sometimes targeting anybody in particular. There's just a million bots trying to take down PHP and loads of things run on PHP. So you've got PHP in your infrastructure and that means you're not taken down, but your servers are struggling under the load. The number of bots that are trying to crawl all kinds of websites and things constitutes effectively a DDoS at the moment, although it's not really a true DDoS.
Right. It's not intentional. It just becomes one by volume.

So it's actually becoming a little bit moot what exactly constitutes a denial of service attack versus merely being under extremely heavy load. I'm sure that the jokes are international about phoning your bank or some other institution and getting a recorded message saying, "We're sorry, we're experiencing an unusual volume of calls at the moment. You are number forty-two in the queue." You've always got that volume of calls. It's not unusual. That's your normal volume of calls. Hire more people. That's web service now, isn't it?

Yes, gosh. But there's that. Aside from maybe the Canonical thing being a bit of an outlier in this broader discussion, it seems like there's not necessarily a single thing to blame here, right? It's very easy to immediately jump to the conclusion that this is AI. Right? They're lying to us.

Well, I think we can establish the cause under the larger umbrella of deferred maintenance because we have this aging, underfunded infrastructure. That was the case with the FAA outage, and we have all of these really old bugs in software that are just now coming to light because AI has gotten so good at finding them in a lot of either commercial projects or open source code that wasn't really built with security top of mind. And so all of these things are now happening right at once. There's this massive need to upgrade infrastructure. There's this need to patch all of these vulnerabilities really quickly before attackers reverse engineer them with AI and then exploit them. And it's creating this perfect storm that looks like it could be an attack, but it's software vulnerabilities, it's deferred maintenance, and that's at least the primary cause of all the outages.

Yes.You don't think... I mean, I'm just going to put my tinfoil hat on and say, "Well, are these people lying to us?" Are they trying to cover up another big wave of OpenAI agents crashing networks due to stupidly miscoded exercises that are escaping sandboxes?
Can I propose a rephrasing of the question?
Yes, they're lying to us, but are they lying about this?

Yes, right. And and that's the thing. I mean, it's always the that's that's always a question at the back of everybody's minds. Like over the weekend I had someone who a friend of mine, she's not involved in cybersecurity, she's not involved in government, and trying to convince me that no, this this was all part of a coordinated cyber attack. And very convinced. Um some people, there's there's a few people in the security industry who are saying, "Well, it seems that they were really quick to rush and say, 'no this was just scheduled downtime or an upgrade that we had planned.'" But the consensus from all of the security folks who are a lot smarter than I am is that no, this doesn't appear to be a coordinated cyber attack. This really does look like it has to do with a bunch of bugs being discovered in all of our interconnected systems.And this has a cascading effect across so many critical systems and services that we all use.
Right. I know you covered this in the story you wrote about the greater impact of all this. Can we expect more of this going forward? I think we probably all know the answer to that.
Yes. It's a definite yes on that one.

That raises the big question of this. I've been telling my family and my friends all along that there's not an indication that this is connected. But it was less than a month ago that the three of us were on here talking about PHP2Shell and how that basically opened the box to us realizing the entire digital sphere that we exist in is held together with duct tape and twine. Yes.

Right. And we see some real attacks too, with the refrigeration attacks and the water system attacks in America over the summer. So there are real attacks that are happening and affecting critical systems too. So it's not like these outages are occurring in a vacuum with nothing being perpetrated by criminals, or spies, or nation-state attackers.

Yes. You think about it like the modern internet that we have... Liam, you lived on the continent for a while. So, in history, Europe was a whole bunch of very small, very isolated communities. They developed their own languages, their own culture, everything. And then they grew and they became one connected mass. But in some ways they still can't talk to each other. And I feel like that's the kind of technology that we have now. We have all these disparate systems that existed as separate entities. The FAA's 50-year-old systems didn't need to be connected to the internet and talking to X, Y, and Z. And now they do. But all those other systems are talking a different language too. So we have a massive technical debt. Every week, with PHP2Shell, the refrigerator attacks, everything. . Every week we turn around and we learn one more way in which there's a huge technical debt that wewe're now in the point where we're like, "oh oops, you know, uh..."

Yes, this is a growing problem. I want to start to wave my arms around and talk about synergistic network effects. I have interviewed some of the people behind the original ARM operating system on The Register and I still attend the meetings of the London Acorn User Group. Over the years they've had some pretty big names in the industry. We had Sophie Wilson, the inventor of the ARM chip, there a couple of times. One time somebody asked a question: "Do you feel happy and proud that there's an ARM chip inside every iPhone and every Android phone?" She laughed at the question, and when the person looked surprised, she said, "There isn't an ARM chip inside every iPhone. There are six or eight ARM chips inside every iPhone." Bear in mind this was more than a decade ago. She said there's a central ARM chip with several cores powering it, but there's an ARM chip in the GSM mobile signaling stack, there's an ARM chip in its USB controller, there's an ARM chip in its memory controller, there's an ARM chip in its Bluetooth controller, because it's cheaper to embed an ARM chip and run a bit of software on it than design dedicated silicon to manage all the different wireless networks. It's all ARM chips all the way down. Your iPhone isn't an ARM device; it's a loose cluster of multiple different ARM devices of different generations. And nobody is entirely sure anymore if they're all running the same stack.

A very visible example of this was in Intel chips until about the early Core 2 Duo era: they had an embedded management processor that was derived from the accelerator in a Nintendo Famicom game from the nineties called Quark. Then Intel replaced it with a cut-down x86 core running Minix, the experimental operating system that inspired Linux. They never gave back any of the code, and the Minix project faltered and is dormant because Dr. Andy Tanenbaum, the guy who founded it, retired. Nowadays in any modern internet-connected server there'll be Linux in its instrumented lights-out monitoring chip. There'll probably be Linux in its network interfaces. There'll be Linux running on the main CPU cluster. I wrote recently about a Linux-powered RISC-V graphics card which runs Ubuntu on loads of RISC-V cores in the GPU.
Are they all on the same Linux version? Have they all been patched against vulnerabilities? No.

"I believe with all my heart that if the federal territories minister were not me, from DAP, this matter would not have been brought into this (special) chamber. I am confident of this.

"We have gazetted (many hectares) of land for protection, but they did not attract the same level of interest.
"But because this involves KLSCAH, a Chinese organisation, and a DAP minister whom they believe approved the reduction, there has been considerable interest," she said.
She said this when winding up the debate on an emergency motion concerning KLSCAH's land at the Special Chamber today.

Yeoh said land matters were governed by the National Land Code and fell under the jurisdiction of the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur Land Committee, chaired by the chief secretary to the government.
"I have no authority over this. I have no authority," she said.
On Nov 14, the government approved a 99-year lease renewal for KLSCAH at a nominal premium of RM1,000, compared with the initial estimate of RM4.67 million.
Yeoh had said on Nov 16 that the reduction took into account the change in the land's designated use from commercial to institutional.
She had said the land was restricted to institutional and heritage purposes, which were among the factors considered when assessing KLSCAH's appeal for a lower premium.
The Federal Territories Land Committee approved the surrender and re-alienation of the land for institutional use on Sept 14.
The decision has since prompted calls for greater transparency over the valuation process and the justification for the reduction.
The KLSCAH building was declared a National Heritage building in 2007, while the National Heritage Department allocated RM500,000 for conservation work in 2008.

1b2a065cf4a0745c: KUANTAN: The Sultan of Pahang will grace the opening of the KotaSAS central station, the first along the 665km East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) alignment tomorrow.
This comes ahead of the project's launching ceremony on Dec 12.
The KotaSAS station is one of 16 stations under the ECRL's first phase, running from Gombak Integrated Transport Terminal in Selangor to Kota Baru.
Notably, the station's project site was also the venue for the ECRL project's groundbreaking ceremony on Aug 9, 2017, by the then prime minister, Datuk Seri Najib Razak.

In a media invitation, project owner Malaysia Rail Link (MRL) said Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah would be accompanied by the Tengku Ampuan of Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah, and the Tengku Mahkota of Pahang, Tengku Hassanal Ibrahim Alam Shah.
Chief Secretary to the Government and MRL chairman Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail are also expected to attend.
Following the opening ceremony, Al-Sultan Abdullah and the VIPs are expected to board the Comprehensive Inspection Train to the Bentong ECRL station before returning to KotaSAS.
The ECRL, which traverses Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang and Selangor, is scheduled to begin operations next month, with ticket sales expected to open soon.
Pahang has seven stations along the alignment, namely Bentong, Kuantan Port City, Cherating, KotaSAS, Paya Besar, Maran, and Temerloh.
Terengganu has six stations in Jerteh, Bandar Permaisuri, Kuala Terengganu, Dungun, Kemasik and Chukai, while Kelantan has two in Kota Baru and Pasir Puteh.
Its extension from Gombak to Port Klang is expected to be operational by January 2028.
9da5458c328abd36: COPENHAGEN: Lego, the world's biggest toymaker by revenue, announced Monday plans to spend US$1.1 billion to build a new factory in Portugal, its eighth worldwide and fourth in Europe.
"We're going to invest in a new factory in Estarreja, Portugal, which will be an investment of over a billion euros," Carsten Rasmussen, the Danish firm's director of operations, told AFP.
Construction will begin in the first half of 2027 in Estarreja, a central coastal town around 50km south of Porto.
"It's an investment that's supporting our long-term growth ambitions... to cater to the European region," he said.
The new plant, the latest addition to Lego's European factories in Denmark, Hungary and the Czech Republic, will start producing bricks in 2030.
It "strengthens our network in Europe with more flexibility, more resilience, strength in our sustainability ambitions, et caetera," Rasmussen said.
"Portugal is a growing manufacturing country," he added, noting that "the economy is growing, we see the skilled labour is really, really good".
Lego opened a factory in Vietnam last year, and in the US it plans to open a new factory and regional distribution centre in 2027.
It also recently announced plans to expand its factory in Mexico by 35%, and is expanding its plants in Hungary and China.
The toymaker, based in Billund in western Denmark, registered its best ever first-half earnings this year.
Present in 54 countries, Lego has around 34,000 employees worldwide, and the new Portugal factory is expected to create more than 1,000 new jobs in the region.
d42052fde9f8eca2: PETALING JAYA: United Nations Population Fund Malaysia (UNFPA Malaysia) has joined the chorus calling for femicide to be recognised and legislated as a distinct crime ahead of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women on Wednesday.
Femicide is the intentional killing of a woman or girl because of her gender.

Citing global statistics, UNFPA Malaysia's assistant representative, Tengku Aira Tengku Razif, said a woman is killed by a partner or family member every 11 minutes, while fewer than one in 10 women who experience violence reports it to the police.
She said Malaysian women are not spared, noting the recent wave of violence towards females, especially young girls.
Several women and girls have been killed between January and October in cases reported in Batu Pahat, Butterworth, Kepong, Kulim, Ketereh, Kuantan and Yong Peng.

"We cannot fix an issue we refuse to name. Recognising femicide as a distinct crime would move Malaysia beyond treating these killings as isolated tragedies, and start naming the pattern behind them,” she told FMT.

Tengku Aira said recognising femicide as a standalone criminal offence, which the likes of the Women’s Aid Organisation and the Human Rights Commission of Malaysia also called for last month, would help bring accountability and justice for the victims.

It would also help with the collation of data that authorities and policymakers would need when it comes to early intervention, protecting survivors, and putting an end to violence before it turns deadly.

The call to recognise femicide as a distinct crime under the law will be the focus at the annual commemoration of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women (IDEVAW) 2026, organised by UNFPA Malaysia, to be held at Hemisfera, Menara Kuala Lumpur, on Nov 25.
It is organised by the UNFPA in Malaysia.
Among those attending are Nikolas Myint, the UN resident coordinator for Malaysia, Singapore and Brunei Darussalam, deputy communications minister Teo Nie Ching, and lawyer Sangeet Kaur Deo.
Tengku Aira said the event will also focus on tech-facilitated gender-based violence, such as using AI to create explicit deepfakes, cyberbullying, and stalking women online.
When it comes to tech-facilitated gender-based violence, she said, an important precedent needs to be set first: safeguarding of individuals' digital likeness and rights.
She said laws are needed to prevent "our likeness, voice, thoughts and personality from being misused or harvested".
"If these can be enshrined legislatively, then it provides a much stronger basis for legal protection," she said.

8f7bb8d4e8be4154: KUALA LUMPUR: A 25-year-old woman was killed after the Honda HR-V she was travelling in crashed into a road divider along Jalan Tuanku Abdul Halim on Friday.

b84f876968e41948: US President Donald Trump has threatened a "tremendous tax" on American companies building datacenters overseas, arguing that the infrastructure should stay at home to preserve the country's AI lead over China.

Speaking at a White House press conference after returning from the Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, Trump portrayed AI leadership as a contest America could not afford to lose.

Trump went on to say that "we're not going to allow our companies to build datacenters outside of our country," adding that "they allowed that to happen with chips and everything else and it was very destructive to our country."
The threat appeared to catch even his own administration unbriefed. "I haven't even said that to my people, but I'm telling them now," Trump said.
The Official White House Rapid Response account posted a video clip on X.
We asked the White House if the president intends to follow through, and we will let you know if we get an answer.
Trump said: "We're not going to allow companies to build datacenters in other countries. If they do that, they can, but we're going to put a tremendous tax on them. We want them to do it here."

The threat comes amid concerns that Chinese entities were able to use Nvidia's cutting-edge GPUs for training AI models by accessing cloud services hosted in third countries. The US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) issued new rules to try and crack down on this practice last week.

"We're not allowing datacenters to go into other countries, as China will take all of them, and we're not allowing that to happen," Trump repeated. "We're going to put tremendous penalties on companies that try and do it. They want to build that one in Finland, and we're not allowing that to happen," he added.
Google is expanding its facilities in Finland, including one recently in the news because the developer had reportedly illegally felled 250,000 trees to make way for it.
Such a policy seems unlikely to be allowed by Congress, where both houses will be under the control of the Democrats when the new term begins in January.
Amazon, Google, and Microsoft already operate global datacenter networks to serve customers in different regions. Restrictions on further overseas construction would complicate those businesses.
Omdia chief analyst Roy Illsley expressed doubt that this is a serious threat.

"There will be ways around that if he does impose some executive order, and the ability to build datacenters is not just an American skill, many countries can build them, it is the equipment in them that is mostly US," he told The Register.

"So I do not take this seriously as it would not work, there is no such thing as a US datacenter, they are made up of thousands of components from all over the globe. He could stop US capital from being invested in those countries, but that could have trade consequences."
Mike Kharchenko of European hosting firm HostZealot said there are good reasons why the cloud giants operate datacenters outside the US, such as latency and regulatory compliance.

"A buyer in Frankfurt won't wait for a page to load from Virginia. Some countries require certain data to stay inside their borders, and big European clients write it into contracts anyway," he stated.
Trump claimed that communities in America that host datacenters are "making so much money that they don't know what to do with it."

Those claimed benefits come alongside substantial public subsidies. Nonprofit organization Good Jobs First reported earlier this year that some states are losing billions in revenue because of the tax abatement schemes offered to companies to entice them to set up shop there. ®
68373b31fad12b07: PETALING JAYA: The Selangor government is in the process of seizing land used as an illegal dumping site in Ijok to address pollution and recurring flood risks, says menteri besar Amirudin Shari.
He said the area, comprising two lots measuring 0.4ha each near the sixth bund of the Sungai Buloh flood mitigation scheme, had been encroached upon for illegal waste disposal activities.

“We are currently in the process of seizing the land, which is expected to be completed by the end of March next year. Action has already been taken, but the process must comply with procedure and will take some time.

“The process takes about six months, in accordance with procedures followed in previous cases. We hope this can be resolved as soon as possible," he was quoted as saying by Bernama after visiting the area today.
Amirudin said that, according to a briefing by the irrigation and drainage department, Sungai Buloh overflowed along a 200m stretch of the embankment on Nov 4 and 17.

“I was informed that the embankment had been damaged twice by the illegal dumpsite operators, causing water to overflow into residential areas. Repair work is under way on a critical 60m section of the embankment,” he said.
Amirudin called on the police to increase patrols around the bund to prevent further damage to the embankment.
He also said legal action would be taken against the landowners, even if they claimed they were unaware of the illegal dumping activities on their properties.
Meanwhile, he said the state government would investigate claims that development near a cemetery in Setia Alam, Shah Alam, had contributed to flooding in Meru last week.

“We will take firm action. If their retention ponds are not functioning, we will issue a stop-work order. I want to ensure they rectify the problem first. Only then will we allow them to resume their operations,” he said.
1e2e3987843429ae: KUALA LUMPUR: Kerajaan tidak berhasrat mewujudkan syarat pelesenan khas buat syarikat penyedia permainan dalam talian seperti yang telah dilaksanakan bagi platform media sosial, kata Timbalan Menteri Komunikasi Teo Nie Ching.

Beliau berkata, Forum Kandungan Komunikasi dan Multimedia Malaysia (CMCF) kini sedang menjalankan kajian bagi menilai perkembangan risiko dan pendekatan kawal selia yang bersesuaian berkaitan perkhidmatan permainan dalam talian.
“Kajian ini merangkumi aspek keselamatan kanak-kanak, interaksi antara pengguna, ciri dan juga kandungan permainan serta langkah perlindungan yang dilaksanakan pemberi perkhidmatan.

“Selain itu, MCMC (Suruhanjaya Komunikasi dan Multimedia Malaysia) turut meneliti amalan antarabangsa sebagai sebahagian daripada penilaian,” katanya ketika menggulung perbahasan Rang Undang-Undang Perbekalan (Belanjawan) 2027 dan Usul Anggaran Perbelanjaan Pembangunan 2027 peringkat jawatankuasa bagi Kementerian Komunikasi di Dewan Rakyat.

Beliau berkata, hasil kajian CMCF akan menjadi asas dalam menentukan sama ada terdapat keperluan memperkenalkan langkah perlindungan atau pendekatan kawal selia tambahan yang bersesuaian dengan konteks Malaysia, dengan mengambil kira perkembangan industri, risiko dikenal pasti serta keberkesanan langkah perlindungan sedia ada.
Setakat ini, katanya, CMCF telah mengadakan rundingan awam bagi membangunkan subkod permainan (gaming subcode) sejak September lepas.

Beliau berkata, ia antara lain melibatkan kumpulan kerja daripada pihak berkepentingan seperti pengendali, aplikasi, pembangun, pemainan tempatan dan antarabangsa, pakar keselamatan dalam talian, industri e-sukan, pengamal undang-undang dan penyelidik.
“Maklum balas yang diterima menerusi rundingan awam ini akan dipertimbangkan bagi menambah baik 'subcode' tersebut," katanya.

“Sebarang keperluan untuk menyemak semula peraturan berkuat kuasa akan dinilai berdasarkan maklum balas pihak berkepentingan, perkembangan semasa, risiko yang dikenal pasti serta keberkesanan kerangka kawal selia sedia ada."

Menurut beliau, pendekatan itu adalah bagi memastikan kawal selia yang dilaksanakan kekal relevan berasaskan bukti dan berkadar dengan risiko, di samping mengutamakan keselamatan pengguna khususnya kanak-kanak dan remaja.

Dewan Rakyat kemudian meluluskan anggaran perbelanjaan mengurus dan pembangunan 2027 berjumlah RM2.613 bilion yang diperuntukkan kepada Kementerian Komunikasi dalam Belanjawan 2027 dengan lebih suara bersetuju, selepas dibahas 19 Ahli Parlimen.
935b6c1912f37160: LOS ANGELES: Jaafar Jackson realised just how hard he had pushed his vocals for the King of Pop's 1979 hit Don't Stop 'Til You Get Enough when he woke up unable to speak the day after filming the scene.

According to AsiaOne yesterday, the 30-year-old star—who plays his late uncle in director Antoine Fuqua's biopic Michael—shared the story on the latest episode of the Los Angeles Times' The Envelope podcast.
Jaafar, the son of Jermaine Jackson, said: "I remember shooting the Don't Stop 'Til You Get Enough scene when I was in the booth with Quincy Jones and [engineer] Bruce Swedien.
"That day, just singing it all falsetto, the very next day my voice was gone. It was lost just from shooting that one scene."

Recreating the recording session, which blends Michael's original vocals with Jaafar's own, gave the young actor a deeper appreciation for the hard work the 13-time Grammy winner put into perfecting his craft.
He said: "It just made me realise, hearing a record, you don't realise the work that goes into doing that and into creating that.

"That one was a tough one on my voice, singing that high. But it was really cool to match, or try to match, Michael's vocal ability in that moment, in that scene, especially with that time, because that song was one of his favourites that he wrote in the early days."

Michael, which charts the Thriller hitmaker's rise from The Jackson 5 to global solo stardom, also required Jaafar to master the late singer's iconic dance routines—a commitment so intense that he danced until his feet bled.
In April, 61-year-old Fuqua recalled to Deadline: "I went over to Havenhurst, where he was living, rehearsing, and practising.
"The walls were covered in Michael, but with detailed graphs, it was like A Beautiful Mind. So, he's in it, but can he do it the day of?
"We started with Bad with a big show on the Sony lot with 1,000 extras and lights, a big show. Here ya go, kid, throw you into the fire. And he blew my mind.
"I watched him do it over and over again with the dance moves, until his feet were bleeding, but also the acting routine."

All that dedication has paid off. Michael has become Lionsgate's biggest release and the first biopic in history to surpass US$1 billion (about RM4.12 billion) at the global box office—a milestone Jaafar believes his uncle, who died in June 2009 aged 50, would have loved.
"I know how proud Michael would be of that, because he was someone who wanted to break many records."

d3947b03ca9aa761: TUMPAT: Desperate to rebuild her life after her husband died, a 31-year-old Myanmar woman risked everything by bringing her 9-month-old daughter along on a dangerous journey into Malaysia.

2f1612e1f6e348fb: PETALING JAYA: Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) chairman Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki disagrees with the education ministry’s plan to place surplus teachers at boarding schools to help ease wardens' workload, saying the ministry should instead emulate Mara’s recruitment of ex-military personnel as wardens.
He said hostel safety required wardens who were trained in emergency and conflict management, prevention of bullying, child protection and scheduled supervision.

“Appointing surplus teachers does not automatically provide these specific competencies. The ministry could also develop a full-time warden career pathway with clear training, performance standards and accountability,” he said in a Facebook post today.

Today, education director-general Azam Ahmad said his ministry planned to increase the number of hostel wardens, including at boarding schools, to ease the workload of teachers who also serve as wardens.
Azam said the ministry was capitalising on the fact that 99% of teacher vacancies had been filled to deploy surplus teachers to schools facing a shortage of hostel wardens.
Asyraf said Malaysia could tap a pool of skilled workers among retired military personnel and police officers.

“They could be considered for professional warden positions, subject to background checks, assessment of their suitability to work with teenagers, and training in pedagogy, psychology and child protection.
“Their experience in discipline and security management could be put to good use, without assuming that all retirees are automatically suitable to serve as wardens.
“Let teachers focus on their primary responsibility of educating students,” he said.

Earlier this year, Mara began appointing ex-military personnel as wardens at all 58 Mara Junior Science Colleges nationwide, following what it described as the success of its pilot project at the Besut and Balik Pulau colleges.
Asyraf previously said a study on the pilot project's effectiveness found a sharp drop in student disciplinary issues, with bullying cases reduced to almost zero.

706d0dd37cd08b1a: KUALA LUMPUR: Kerajaan tidak dapat meneruskan siasatan terhadap dakwaan wujudnya kempen kecerdasan buatan (AI) untuk mempengaruhi pengundi kerana firma teknologi AS, Anthropic, masih belum memberi respons terhadap permohonan maklumat, kata Timbalan Menteri Komunikasi Teo Nie Ching.

Teo berkata, Suruhanjaya Komunikasi dan Multimedia Malaysia (MCMC) memerlukan bahan bukti untuk menjalankan siasatan lanjut, dan menggesa Ahli Parlimen yang mempunyai maklumat supaya berkongsinya dengan badan kawal selia itu.

Beliau berkata demikian di Dewan Rakyat bagi menjawab soalan Wan Saiful Wan Jan (PN-Tasek Gelugor) tentang mengapa kementerian tidak mempunyai sebarang perkembangan terkini sejak jawapan Parlimen pada 11 Nov lepas.

Wan Saiful turut mempersoalkan mengapa kerajaan tidak membuat laporan berhubung dakwaan Anthropic bahawa ada pihak yang meminta sejuta tontonan palsu untuk akaun media sosial Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim.
Teo berkata isu tontonan palsu itu ialah perkara berasingan daripada dakwaan yang sedang disiasat MCMC.
Tambahan, katanya, MCMC tidak menguruskan akaun media sosial Anwar.
Dalam laporan pada 10 Sept lepas, Anthropic memaklumkan pihaknya telah melumpuhkan sebuah platform manipulasi pilihan raya komersial yang terutamanya menyasarkan rakyat Malaysia.

Operasi itu melibatkan kira-kira 1,000 akaun media sosial palsu, selain laman berita palsu dan dosier perisikan rekaan, serta menggunakan model AI Claude milik Anthropic untuk membina sistem yang boleh memprofilkan dan menyasarkan pengundi Malaysia mengikut kawasan pilihan raya.

Anthropic turut menyatakan ada pihak yang meminta sejuta tontonan palsu untuk akaun Anwar, namun tidak mengaitkan Anwar atau pejabatnya dengan permintaan itu mahupun menyatakan sama ada tontonan berkenaan berjaya dipenuhi.
Teo berkata, platform media sosial telah menurunkan 202,402 hantaran berkaitan penipuan dan kandungan lain antara 1 Jan hingga 15 Nov, atas permintaan MCMC.
Jumlah itu meningkat sebanyak 31,769 dalam tempoh sebulan sejak 15 Okt.
Beliau berkata, polis bertanggungjawab menyiasat kes penipuan dalam talian, manakala perkara berkaitan mendapatkan semula wang yang lesap berada di luar bidang kuasa kementerian.

362b561c4f5d2c55: The farmer-poet Wendell Berry once described a dystopian world where society is singularly directed toward “the objective” – a relentless drive for industrial extraction that leads to the destruction of nature and communities. The idea captured Berry’s concerns about the industrialization of agriculture and the expansion of natural resource extraction that became prominent across rural America in the latter decades of the 20th century. Over nine decades, Berry watched how agribusinesses’ and farm owners’ pursuit of productive efficiency and maximum profits led to machines and synthetic chemicals replacing human farm labor, and the replacement of diversified farms with monocropping and concentrated animal-feeding operations. Across the U.S., he saw small farms disappear, often consolidated into vast corporate businesses with absent owners. What gets lost in this pursuit of production and profit, he noted, are community, human dignity and flourishing, natural beauty and ecological well-being. People are the heart of rural towns, like Waubeka, Wis. Farm consolidation has shrunk many of America’s rural towns since the mid 1900s. AP Photo/Teresa Crawford As agriculture researchers and rural sociologists, we, like Berry, have seen how the industrialization of agriculture has changed the face of rural America and hollowed out its communities. Once-thriving main streets in rural towns have slowly lost their businesses, with fewer farm-related jobs to keep local residents in the area. Machine dealers and suppliers of farm input such as seeds, fertilizer and pesticides have disappeared. Local grocery stores have been replaced by gas station convenience stores. Schools have shrunk or consolidated with the population decline. Hospitals have closed. This “unsettling of America,” in Berry’s words, shows that the farm economy and the rural economy no longer rise and fall together. Rural communities continue to decline despite farm booms and busts. Losing farming’s rural economy multiplier effect Since the late 1940s, the number of farmers in the U.S. has plummeted by nearly 90%, falling from 5.9 million in 1948 to only 715,000 by 2025. During the same period, the agricultural workforce has shifted from mostly farm owners – about 78% – with a few hired hands in 1948 to one today where most of the work is done by farm laborers, about 68% of the workforce. This means profits from farming mainly flow to a small number of farm owners, while the people doing the farm work are paid much less. The loss of small, owner-operated farms, where a farm family could make a living, is one reason many rural communities have lost population over the past century. In prior eras, farming energized rural communities as money circulated in the rural economy, supporting rural businesses and populations – what is termed a “multiplier effect.” Today, local suppliers and services are harder to find, and farm profits instead flow to owners outside the community. Agriculture today resembles capital-intensive natural resource extraction, like mining, where a small number of very profitable businesses operate most acres in the county. Such farms employ few people at low wages, and profits accrue to distant landlords and investment firms. This shift further reinforces rural decline. The farm economy of the 21st century does little to create additional jobs in rural America. An analysis of 11 counties in Iowa found that every US$1 million of agricultural sales creates 2.4 total farm jobs and 1.6 spin-off jobs in other nonfarm businesses, for a total of four new jobs. By contrast, healthcare creates 10 new jobs and construction creates seven new jobs in all for every $1 million in sales. Both pay good wages, which keeps rural people from leaving and helps rural economies thrive. Both also create more spin-off jobs. In short, agriculture produces profits for the company, whereas healthcare and construction produce good-paying jobs for rural residents. More small farms can help communities thrive In the mid-1940s, the U.S. Senate commissioned two studies on the social impacts of economic concentration and corporate monopolies. In one, Walter Goldschmidt, an anthropologist at the University of California, Berkeley, described two agricultural communities in California, one with a few large farms and the other with numerous smaller farms. He evaluated the social qualities of each and found that the community with more small farms had a higher standard of living and quality of life than the community with a few large farms. The other study, overseen by Columbia sociology professor C. Wright Mills, compared urban manufacturing areas in the Midwest. It found that locations with many small companies had a more robust economic life, with higher socioeconomic well-being, than areas dominated by a few large firms. Many rural sociologists have tested these findings since then. One, a Cornell study led by rural sociologist Thomas Lyson, found a way to counter the effects of farm consolidation. Using U.S. Census of Agriculture and other county-level data, it found that communities with large-scale industrial-style farms that also had politically active populations and a high percentage of people running small, independent businesses tended to have higher levels of social well-being than those without. The effect of economic concentration Looking at the agriculture sector in 2026, it’s clear that policymakers have not listened to the concerns raised by Berry or the rural sociologists. According to the latest Census of Agriculture, America had fewer than 2 million farms in 2022. Fewer than 6% of those farms accounted for over three-quarters of all agricultural production. Farms are getting larger and more specialized. Economist Jim MacDonald documented that half of all cropland in 2017 was on farms with 1,445 acres, more than double the 650 acres in 1987. Half of all dairy farms had more than 1,300 cows in 2017, up from 80 in 1987. Half of all pig farms in 1987 marketed 1,200 pigs or more – the midpoint is currently over 50,000 pigs per year. The number of American farms fell while the size of those farms grew as consolidation became common across the country in the second half of the 20th century. USDA The supply chain is also shrinking, leaving farmers with fewer choices. Today, fewer companies control more of the markets where farmers buy their fertilizers and pesticides or sell their products, which means that farmers have less control over what they can raise or sell. For instance, just two companies accounted for 71.6% of the U.S. corn seed market in 2018-2022, and those same two companies accounted for 65.9% of the soybean seed market, according to USDA researchers. Twenty years earlier, the top two companies in those markets accounted for 47.2% of the corn seed market and 41.8% of the soybean seed market. When four or fewer firms control 40% or more of a market, farmers tend to pay more for seeds, fertilizer and pest control and receive less for their commodities, while consumers continue to face higher prices. Consolidation of land and commodity markets at the farm level often goes unnoticed and sometimes undocumented. University of Iowa economist Silvia Secchi describes how changes in the U.S. Census of Agriculture in 2002 and in 2017 “obfuscates the degree of consolidation” in the farm sector by allowing farms to report up to three or four farm operators. These changes have led to the official count of over 3 million farm operators, even though there are fewer than 2 million farms. By looking at the volume of sales, Secchi found that fewer than half of these 2 million farms produce commodities worth more than $1,000 annually. She contends that this way of counting farmers does a double disservice to small farm operators. First, it lumps disadvantaged farmers into a group that includes retired farmers and farmland owners who might be using their land as a tax write-off. Second, when the overall farm incomes are averaged, the inclusion of these small farmers make the large, high-value farmers appear to need more federal support. How to improve conditions in farm country Restoring the vibrant rural farm economy of the past may be unrealistic, but some policies could at least improve conditions. Devising new – and enforcing existing – antitrust laws to break up oligopolies and monopolies in the materials farms need, such as seeds and fertilizer, as well as in processing and trade could give farmers more choices about what to raise and where to sell it, while protecting consumers from high prices. Irrigated fields stretch for miles in many rural farming regions across the middle of America, including on Colorado’s eastern plains. Jim Wark /Design Pics Editorial/Universal Images Group via Getty Images) Right-to-repair laws could help farmers gain more control over their expensive machinery. Farm subsidies could be directed to smaller farmers who produce food – many of whom were inspired by Berry to become farmers – rather than toward the largest farmers who produce a few commodities at a massive scale. And finally, policymakers can develop rural policies that actually invest in the rural environment and communities, rather than simply subsidizing commodities in ways that primarily benefit the corporate owners of vast areas of farmland. 41496c8a0956b93d: Tech stocks are on a bumpy ride, weighed down by the slump in Nvidia's shares. Liu Yanan/Xinhua via Getty ImagesAfter stock markets, including the tech-heavy NASDAQ, got pummeled on Nov. 20, 2026, many Americans are asking themselves whether the huge bet on artificial intelligence is heading south. This question has profound implications for retirement savings, given how much these investment accounts are tied to stocks. The NASDAQ has plunged about 18% since early October and has lost more than US$4 trillion since Nov. 16. The broad-based S&P also took a beating and has now shed all its gains for the year. As a finance professor and certified financial planner, I can’t tell you whether the bubble has truly burst for good. But I can explain how the default model that most 401(k) plans use works, where it protects you, and what you might consider changing. Whether AI stocks recover or not, the steps that protect a retirement account are the same: Know what you own, keep the mix of assets in balance, and hold enough in savings and low-risk funds to cover the years when you’ll need it. Here are some basic facts to guide your planning. Many Americans are saving on autopilot Most 401(k) savers hold a target-date fund, which is named for the year of your “target” retirement and is often chosen as a default option by the employer. To understand how the current stock market volatility affects retirement savings, it’s important to first explain how these funds work. About 55% of U.S. families have a defined contribution retirement account, such as a 401(k) or an individual retirement account. And inside a 401(k), the investing is increasingly done for you. Six in 10 plans administered by the fund giant Vanguard signed workers up automatically in 2025 when they started a new job. And when those plans set a default investment, 98% of savers choose a target-date fund. About 60% of the nearly 5 million savers in those plans held a single target-date fund and nothing else. Taken together, target-date funds now hold $4.8 trillion. Inside each target-date fund is a list of index funds, which are named so because they track a particular market index. Vanguard’s series, the largest, is built mainly from four indices: U.S. stocks, international stocks, U.S. bonds and international bonds. The mix changes the older the saver gets, gradually moving away from high-return, high-risk stocks to safer, lower-yielding bonds. For example, Vanguard’s 2055 fund was just over 91% stocks at the end of September 2026, reflecting the relative youth of those holding it. That share drops to 16% for savers invested in the 2027 fund, who expect to retire imminently. The idea of target-date funds is that you can put your retirement savings on autopilot, with the mix of stocks and bonds getting more conservative the older you get. Brano on Unsplash Tech volatility is forcing new questions That autopilot model is now being tested, starting with Nvidia. In the span of a week, Nvidia went from riding the AI boom to getting mired in crisis. On Nov. 5, after the U.S. midterm elections raised the prospect of new curbs on AI and data centers, Nvidia shares fell more than 9%, while the broad-based S&P 500 index lost 4.4%. Then, on Nov. 12, Nvidia announced that CEO Jensen Huang had resigned. By the end of that week, Nvidia had lost more than $1 trillion in market value within a month. It’s too early to say whether the AI bubble is over. Some analysts argue that it’s just losing some air rather than bursting. But as tech stocks, especially Nvidia, continue to slide, savers may wonder whether a retirement plan on autopilot should adjust to this fresh volatility. Target-date funds have significant tech exposure Target-date funds are marketed as broadly diversified, often holding thousands of stocks, and financial advisers repeated that point after Huang’s exit. But those stocks aren’t held in equal amounts. Index funds weight companies by market value. So as the value of AI-linked companies soared, their share has grown in the funds most 401(k) savers hold. And that gets to the question of whether there’s a tech bubble riding on overvalued AI companies. By the end of 2025, the 10 largest companies made up nearly 41% of the S&P 500, according to RBC Wealth Management. Yet those 10, almost all of which are in tech and AI, were expected to produce only about 32% of the index’s 2025 earnings. In other words, investors are paying a premium for these shares because they’re expecting great profits later. Bad news can shrink that premium quickly. Savers should also know that a target-date fund dilutes the concentration of AI stocks, but it doesn’t remove them. At the end of September, the 10 largest companies made up 36% of Vanguard’s total U.S. stock fund, with Nvidia at 7%. A 2055 fund keeps about 55% of its money there. So roughly 20 cents of every dollar was riding on 10 companies, and about 4 cents on Nvidia. That means even a small drop in these stocks can have a big impact on your fund, depending on its asset mix. And while diversification hedges against one company’s turmoil, it’s less helpful if there’s a broad repricing of tech stocks. Even in Vanguard’s international fund, the four largest holdings are all tied to chipmaking, led by Taiwan Semiconductor, which makes Nvidia’s chips. Furthermore, diversification doesn’t mean guaranteed protection all the time. In 2008, during the global financial crisis, funds built for people retiring in 2010 lost nearly 24% on average. What to check now if you own a target-date fund In principle, savers don’t need to do anything as long as they choose to stay on autopilot until retirement. Fund managers buy and sell assets to stick to the target mix – a practice known as rebalancing. But rebalancing resets only the broad categories rather than trimming one particular company for growing too large. As Nvidia’s share of the market rose, so did its share of the fund. For people who hold just one target-date fund, I believe the right response to this month’s news is to leave their 401(k) account alone. The fund has been rebalancing all along, and your stake in any one company is modest. When markets are jumpy, savers should review the funds they hold and consider rebalancing toward lower risk if they’re close to retiring. Towfiqu Barbhuiya on Unsplash, CC BY But a saver still needs to check three things. First, consider the year you expect to retire. If you want to move it earlier or later, or want more or less risk, you should choose a fund with a different year. Second, look at what the fund’s share of stocks is today, which is on the fund’s fact sheet. If you’re 60 and your fund is 60% stocks, a 30% fall in stocks would cut your balance by roughly 18%. If that would derail your retirement plans, you can switch to an earlier-dated fund that holds less in stocks and brings less risk. Third, if you have other funds, you should review them. About 1 in 4 target-date investors in Vanguard plans hold other funds. If you add a tech fund or an S&P 500 fund, your account is riskier and more concentrated than the label suggests. What to do if you hold other funds About 31% of savers in Vanguard plans opt out of target-date funds and choose their own investments, perhaps because they find target-date funds too conservative or their fees too costly. For these investors, and for anyone with old 401(k)s and IRAs, there is more to do. Start by looking at the fact sheet for each fund, like this one for Vanguard’s S&P 500 index fund, and compare the top holdings. An S&P 500 index fund, a large-cap growth fund and a technology or Nasdaq-tracking fund look like three investments. But in fact you may own the same handful of companies three times. Next, you should rebalance your holdings according to your plan, not to a prediction. That means returning to the mix of stocks and bonds that you chose in the first place. Trades inside a 401(k) don’t trigger taxes, and many plans offer automatic rebalancing. If yours doesn’t, a simple rule backed by Vanguard research works: review once or twice a year, and rebalance whenever any part of your mix drifts more than about 5 percentage points from your target. Finally, consider broadening the stocks you own. Morningstar Indexes strategist Dan Lefkovitz has pointed to U.S. value stocks, smaller companies and international stocks as areas with less AI exposure. Your plan may offer funds for each. None of these makes you immune to losses, and diversifying can mean trailing the hottest part of the market for years. But the pattern can flip quickly: International stocks gained about 29% in 2025, far ahead of the S&P 500’s 16%. Align your savings to your timeline How much this month’s news matters depends on when you’ll need the money. If you’re decades from retirement, a downturn can work in your favor, because every paycheck contribution buys shares at lower prices. Keep contributing and capture your full employer match. My own research with a colleague has found that accounts on systematic investment plans akin to 401(k)s earned better market-adjusted returns than accounts funded with lump sums. If you’re within 5-10 years of retirement, the bigger danger is what planners call sequence-of-returns risk: A large loss right before or just after you start withdrawing can permanently shrink what your savings can support. A good defense is to hold several years of expected withdrawals in lower-risk assets, such as bonds or money market funds, so you’re never forced to sell stocks after a drop. For retirees, Morningstar’s Christine Benz suggests one to two years of withdrawals in cash and five to eight more in bonds. What not to do The costliest mistake is usually the most tempting: selling everything and waiting for the dust to settle. During the 2008-09 financial crisis, about 117,000 Fidelity 401(k) participants moved entirely out of stocks. Those who stayed out saw their balances grow just 2% by mid-2011, while those who kept some stock exposure saw balances rise 50% on average. Other moves to avoid include stopping your own 401(k) contributions, chasing whatever theme looks safe this month, and pulling money out early, which can mean taxes, penalties and a locked-in loss. Last, don’t hand the decision to a chatbot. It will likely give you sound general guidance, such as diversifying and not panic-selling, and that consensus advice is where AI is reliable. But it is weakest on high-stakes questions that turn on your own situation. 5e97e1e850688270: KUALA LUMPUR: The reduction of the land premium to a nominal rate of RM1,000 for the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall (KLSCAH) was made in accordance with the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur Land Rules 1995.

Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said the nominal rate was set after the land use condition for KLSCAH was amended to allow only institutional buildings, rather than commercial use.
She said the decision also took into account KLSCAH's agreement to convert the land tenure from leasehold to freehold, following its appeal for a reduction in the premium submitted on March 3.

She said the Kuala Lumpur Land Committee meeting on April 23 subsequently deferred consideration of the appeal and agreed that the Federal Territories Lands and Mines Office director should hold discussions with KLSCAH.
"Further discussions were held on June 9 to better understand KLSCAH's circumstances, given that its land is designated a National Heritage Site.

"KLSCAH subsequently expressed its intention to withdraw the appeal and submitted an application to surrender and realienate the land to enable it to be granted for use by a non-governmental organisation.
"In general, under land laws, the state authority has the power to consider applications for the surrender and realienation of land under Sections 197 and 76 of the National Land Code respectively.

"Through these two provisions, KLSCAH applied to convert the land tenure to freehold and amend the land-use condition to allow only institutional buildings," she said when winding up the debate on an emergency motion concerning KLSCAH's land in Special Chamber at the Dewan Rakyat today.
Yeoh said the nominal rate of RM1,000 "did not come from the sky or from assumptions", but was based on Rule 10 of the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur Land Rules 1995.
She said Rule 8C stipulates that land alienated for a place of worship is subject to a premium of RM3,000 per hectare or part thereof.
"The National Land Code and Rule 8C of the Federal Territory Land Rules clearly provide for this premium.
"Rule 8E stipulates that if the alienation is for public use by the federal government or an Islamic religious council, the premium is charged at the nominal rate of RM1,000 per lot," she said.
She also denied influencing the decision to change the land's status and reduce the premium, saying the KL Land Executive Committee made it.

"The chief secretary to the government chairs this meeting, not the federal territories minister from DAP, while the deputy senior secretary of the Prime Minister's Department serves as deputy chairman.

"The attorney-general, treasury secretary-general, Lands and Mines director-general, the Federal Territories Department director-general and the city mayor or their representatives, also sit on the committee.
"All of them are Malays. There is no one from DAP, and no Chinese, on the Land Committee that approved this (KLSCAH) application," she said.

9f9c5655fbcc725f: LAS VEGAS: F1 stars don't need e-hailing services when they have John Wick around!

dd016f0a8d9fc246: KUALA SELANGOR: Kerajaan Negeri Selangor sedang melaksanakan proses merampas tanah yang digunakan sebagai tapak pembuangan sampah haram di kawasan Ijok, di sini bagi menangani isu pencemaran dan risiko banjir yang berulang.

63b3c1a485caf424: KUALA LUMPUR: Federal territories minister Hannah Yeoh has denied unilaterally deciding to allow the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall (KLSCAH) to renew its lease for another 99 years at a nominal premium.

98b7db1f57aadf85: A recent update broke attachment handling for some New Outlook users, prompting Microsoft to recommend switching to the web or Classic version of its email client.

Things are going swimmingly for New Outlook, the email client that Microsoft would very much like users to migrate to. A code change meant that for some users, opening or uploading email attachments failed. It took the company two attempts to fix the problem.

Microsoft confirmed there were issues on November 20, as reports that customers were having problems with attachments began rolling in. By the end of the day, the company had added inline images in email to the litany of woe and "paused the rollout of a recent client update that may be contributing to attachment failures."
The advice for affected users was to switch to the web version, or use Outlook Classic to open or upload attachments and view inline images.

The good news was that Microsoft produced a fix. The bad news was that this fix only resolved problems with Office attachments and inline images, leaving other attachment types affected, according to incident notice EX1561765.
The Windows behemoth tried again with a "supplemental fix" and reported the remaining problems resolved on November 21.
Users needed to close and reopen New Outlook for the fix to take effect.

Microsoft said it had tested the fixes before deployment. Administrators might reasonably wish the original update had received the same attention. The preliminary root cause was a "recent update to the code which supports embedded web content unexpectedly caused impact."

The clock is ticking for Outlook Classic. Microsoft is clear that New Outlook is the future, though Classic Outlook will remain available until at least 2029. The fact that the company had to suggest that affected users fall back on the old warhorse to perform that rarely used email activity – attachment handling – is less than confidence-inspiring.
Still, by the time Outlook Classic is finally put out to pasture, we're sure Microsoft's habit of sending out broken updates will also be a thing of the past. Right? ®
13d0c23472a04e8e: Microsoft has issued a critical vulnerability advisory after attackers were caught raiding Azure API Management (APIM) instances for secrets and performing admin operations.

According to a nonpublic advisory, seen by The Register, Microsoft said the attacks, which have already affected two major energy companies, only impact customers on Azure API Management Classic tiers, not Azure API Management v2.

It said of the now-patched vuln: "Our investigation found that customers were exposed and an unauthorized party could have used the issue to access secrets stored in Azure API Management Classic instances before Microsoft identified the security issue."
Microsoft linked exposure to Classic-tier configurations that did not follow its network security guidance or stored secrets directly in APIM rather than referencing them from Azure Key Vault.
Microsoft directs customers to its security guidance for the recommended configuration.

The advisory lists potentially exposed secrets, including named values, client secrets associated with identity providers and OpenID Connect providers, subscription keys, and tokens used to call direct management APIs.
Security expert Anders Kristiansen warned that stolen credentials could also give attackers access to services behind APIM.

"If someone obtains a credential from that configuration, they may be able to use it directly against the service it protects, outside APIM," he wrote. "What they can reach depends on the credential's permissions and whether it is still valid."
Norway's National Security Authority (NSM) urged organizations using APIM to assume their secrets and named values had been exposed and rotate all tokens and secrets.
The agency also advised mapping the information accessible through each APIM instance to assess the potential scope of any compromise.
NSM credited Norway's energy sector with first detecting the vulnerability last week. It named gas giant Equinor and hydropower company Skagerak Energi among the affected organizations.
The authority commended Equinor for its early detection and rapid information-sharing, and warned that growing use of AI increased the risk of further exploitation.

"The vulnerability affects several sectors in Norway and also beyond Norway's borders," it said. "NSM has close dialogue and cooperation with national and international partners and businesses about the situation.

"When a vulnerability becomes known, multiple actors will be able to attempt to exploit it. Rapid escalation in the use of artificial intelligence is affecting the situation. This poses a risk to Norwegian businesses."
Customers who spoke to The Register warned that forgotten development and test instances could leave more organizations exposed. The extent of exploitation remains unclear.
Microsoft said it identified the security issue on November 18 and automatically applied a mitigation to close the access path the following day.
The Windows giant said customers still needed to investigate whether their instances had been compromised before the mitigation was applied.
NSM nevertheless advised organizations to check their instance's runtime version against its published patch thresholds and contact their provider if it remained unpatched.
Microsoft did not immediately respond to our request for comment. ®
